projects.title: Himawari
projects.tagline: A live video wallpaper for macOS that turns into your music.
projects.what: A macOS menu-bar app that plays any video as your wallpaper and, while a song plays, shows the album's animated cover with hi-fi gear from any era beside it, whose meters follow the real music. Songs without an animated cover get their cover on a record, a cassette, a game cartridge or a hologram. Synced lyrics appear on the gear's display and, with a karaoke sweep, under the cover.
projects.interesting: Skins are small JSON files you can write yourself, and design files lay out whole new eras from blocks; both reload as you save. It updates itself from its GitHub releases in one click. The project page is a playable hi-fi deck with optional synthesized sound effects.
facts: macOS 14.4 or newer, Apple silicon and Intel

image.alt: Neon heads-up-display panels either side of a song's cover projected as a hologram, with the lyric being sung underneath

projects.title: Abiogenesis
projects.tagline: A Rust simulation of how life could arise from non-living matter.
projects.what: A small, plain-language simulation written in Rust with egui, shipped as one self-contained app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Molecules drift in a pool that dries and refills; amino acid chains mutate and recombine; droplets (protocells) form where chains crowd; RNA-like strands build themselves from nucleotides, copy themselves into their complement and compete on fitness.
projects.interesting: The project page has a live soup running the same rules, an animation for every stage, a lineage tree drawn from the simulation's event log and optional synthesized sound effects. Version 0.3.0 covers stages 1 to 3 of a six-stage roadmap.
facts: Live soup, lineage tree, a picture per stage

projects.title: Calendar
projects.tagline: A desktop calendar for people who live in more than one timezone.
projects.what: Keep as many calendars as you like, each in its own timezone, add single, all-day and recurring events, copy them between calendars with timezone conversion, and import or export CSV and iCal. Use it from a graphical interface, an interactive prompt or a script file. It began as a team project in Programming Design Paradigms.
projects.interesting: The same model sits behind all three ways of using it. A Rust port with the same MVC structure has started: the model layer is done, with the Java model tests ported. The project page is a working model of the app as a 1980s office desktop, with a terminal that runs a subset of the real command language.

status.label: Java app out, Rust port started

facts: Java 11 or newer: GUI, prompt and script modes
Phase 1 (model layer) done, command parser next

image.alt: A one-bit calendar window titled Calendar 1.0, with the line: Java original, Rust port under way

projects.title: Atlas-Mobile
projects.tagline: One spec, two native gym apps: SwiftUI on iOS and Compose on Android.
projects.what: A gym progress tracker: check in and see who is where, a lift journal (sets, reps, 1-rep max, personal best), a calorie diary, rankings and friends. It started as a Java Android app for a Human Computer Interaction course at UBC Okanagan, built by a team of five, and was rewritten natively for iOS and Android.
projects.interesting: Both apps keep their logic in a small core module and run every case in one shared spec file, so the two stay in step without a simulator. The project page lets you use a phone drawn in CSS, switch between the two platform looks and run the spec in the browser, even against a model of the old Java bug.
facts: Friends and leaderboard are placeholder data; no backend yet

image.alt: Atlas: one spec, two native gym apps, drawn as an iOS and an Android phone

projects.title: FocusLock
projects.tagline: A minimal macOS focus timer that pauses when an LLM program or a social site takes over.
projects.what: A focus timer with a watchdog that pauses the clock when LLM programs are running or a browser lands on a filtered site, and emergency exits so it can never lock you in. It is designed to be ADHD-friendly.
projects.interesting: The source is private for now, so the project page describes behaviour only. It holds a pretend Mac you can use: a session simulator, a probe that judges look-alike domains and background tabs against your rules, and the emergency exits to practise.
facts: Private; only the project page is public
Session simulator, filter probe, exits you can try

image.alt: FocusLock: a timer plus a distraction blocker, nothing else, with a timer reading 18:00

projects.title: LucasCheck
projects.tagline: A mock sporting-goods store you can check out of, and the tables behind it.
projects.what: The COSC 304 (Introduction to Database Systems) term project of Group 4, rebuilt in 2026 on Next.js 16 and Postgres for Vercel. Browse products, fill a cart, log in with a sample account, check out, and use an admin tab to ship orders.
projects.interesting: The project page is the store in miniature plus the database: an animated diagram of the tables, three walkthroughs of the queries a click touches, and a then-and-now comparison of the course project and the rebuild.

image.alt: A price tag reading Lucas-Check, sporting goods, beside a small database diagram

projects.title: CV and ML Town
projects.tagline: A walkable town that is the hub for my vision and machine learning projects.
projects.what: One side-scrolling street with buildings you walk into. Two projects live there. The ECG project trains a 1D ResNet for multi-label diagnosis on PTB-XL and probes whether it relies on rhythm or on beat shape by shuffling segments. The taxi project predicts NYC trip duration and tip, from a baseline to LightGBM and an MLP, with evaluation under temporal shift.
projects.interesting: The interesting part of the ECG work is the probe: instead of only reporting a score, it asks what the model is using. The town has a map, a plain text version of every place, a stop-motion switch and optional sound.
facts: Map, text version, keyboard and touch controls

image.alt: A green ECG trace above a dotted taxi route between two points

projects.title: Manifold search
projects.tagline: My independent research in computational geometry: shortest paths over curved surfaces.
projects.what: Shortest paths over curved surface meshes, and a coarse-to-fine search that answers them faster. Part 1 was the Algorithms (CS 5800) project: sphere and torus meshes, Dijkstra and A* baselines, and a two-level patch search, benchmarked in a notebook.
projects.interesting: Part 2 is my own continuation as computational geometry: irregular and real meshes, scaling up, what controls the error, and comparison with established geodesic methods. It is research in progress, so no headline claims are made here.
facts: Code and tests in the repository

image.alt: A wireframe sphere with a path drawn across it between two points

projects.title: BIOT 6900 report
projects.tagline: A coursework report on Alzheimer's disease, from genes to drug targets.
projects.what: The coursework for AI-Powered Biotech Workflows, written up like a medical report: a summary of findings, one section per module with lab-style result tables and flags, and the report PDFs. A second deliverable covers drug response and variant interpretation.
projects.interesting: The figures are interactive, including 3D AlphaFold structures you can turn, and the page has a folder-opening intro, a theme switch and optional sounds.
facts: AI-Powered Biotech Workflows: From Discovery to Clinic

projects.title: Agentic code generation
projects.tagline: A multi-stage code-generation pipeline with a compiler in the loop.
projects.what: A multi-stage agentic code-generation pipeline with LLM orchestration and compiler-in-the-loop verification, built as a volunteer at CACTILab since March 2026.
projects.interesting: It implements model tiering, per-turn cost observability and a multi-agent verification loop, so the compiler's verdict feeds back into the next generation turn.
facts: CACTILab, as a volunteer since March 2026
Described here only; no public page or repository

projects.title: The Garage
projects.tagline: A workshop page for small tools, experiments and class projects.
projects.what: Tools and experiments hang on a pegboard, class projects sit in a tool chest, private projects stay in a locked toolbox (described, never linked) and a logbook records the history of projects and their old names. It opens with a roller door and has optional synthesized workshop sounds.
projects.interesting: It holds two macOS tools: DepDeck, a menu-bar manager for Homebrew, npm and cargo packages, and Desktop Shell, which adds a Windows-XP-style taskbar and Start menu and iOS-style desktop folders and widgets. Adding a project is a data edit.
facts: XP-style taskbar and desktop for macOS

projects.title: nextcube terminal
projects.tagline: A NeXTSTEP-style virtual Unix shell with a reverse-engineering CTF.
projects.what: A terminal that runs in the browser as a small virtual Unix system, with a capture-the-flag hidden in its filesystem. It is the terminal on this site's Workbench.
projects.interesting: The site is split into small panels, and the Workbench is where this one lives; it is embedded in a frame and served from its own repository.
facts: The Workbench panel of this site
